findings.summary: Request acceptance and call admission are not atomic. Two concurrent submissions of the same identity can both pass _find_request before either appends, creating duplicate queued requests and Goal calls. Distinct submissions can append A then B durably but enqueue B then A, violating stable journal order. Likewise, two next_goal_call callers can both pass the inflight check and pop separate requests before claim_call; the losing caller raises after removing its request, leaving that request unserved until reconstruction. The journal lock protects individual operations, not these transitions. Serialize per-goal deduplication/acceptance/queue insertion and mode/fence/queue admission, and add barrier-controlled offline regressions. These are development-stage violations of behaviors 1, 2 and 7 and P5/P6, not deferred live Runtime scenarios.

Continuous independently records APPROVE for implementation subject 6ddd7bffb27b311ea33061e61cf9c10a4a19c613. Final independently records REJECT for the request-transition defect above. The previous Final version-activation finding is addressed in the inspected source: activate_version and approve/reject admission through delivery share _version_lock, with an offline concurrency regression.
